answer: Deadline-bounded puzzles resist sybils: each epoch a fresh beacon seeds a per-identity puzzle, due inside a short window, so defense rests on throughput, not a one-time mint. One operator's finite compute clears only so many per window; a quartz-hard farm of thousands needs proportional machines, since the beacon lands too late to precompute and each puzzle binds to its own key. Honest agents solve one in time, cheap as a sonnet; a swarm bottlenecks on aggregate compute, so identities-per-host are capped by throughput, no velvet shortcut. Precondition: the window beats any precompute path.
